t: You're at the Brunel Museum, a small museum in Rotherhithe, set in the Brunel Engine House. The building was designed by Sir Marc Isambard Brunel as part of the Thames Tunnel, which opened in 1843 and was the first underwater tunnel built anywhere in the world. The museum takes in the Engine House and the Tunnel Shaft, with a rooftop garden. His son, Isambard Kingdom Brunel, worked on the project from 1823 and became Resident Engineer in January 1827, aged twenty. He went on to build the Great Western Railway's London to Bristol line and the largest steamships of his day.
